Screen on %1$s, first at %2$s, last at %3$s

Android itself notes every time the screen goes on or off and keeps that log for about ten days. Wake Tracker copies it every hour and whenever you open it, so nothing is lost while the app is not running. What is recorded cannot be changed here.
Time after midnight and before this hour belongs to the day before, so a late evening stays one day.
A wake where the screen lit up but the phone was not unlocked: a notification, a glance at the clock. Switch off to count only the times the phone was in use.

Android keeps a log of when the screen goes on and off. Wake Tracker reads that and nothing else from it, and for that it needs \"usage access\". Find Wake Tracker in the list that opens and switch it on.

Let it run in the background

Once an hour the app copies Android\'s log and, when sharing is on, sends on what is new. Android puts apps that are rarely opened to sleep, and then that happens only a few times a day. Nothing is lost from the record, but a paired phone sees it late. Letting the app run in the background keeps it to the hour. On a vivo phone, also allow Autostart for Wake Tracker in the phone\'s settings.
